project.title: aquascape-wood-orthos-v3
project.description: Orthographic front/right/top construction study from the generated V2 master. Fix single-view inferred thickness before rebuilding 3D.
project.art_direction: Source-matched naturalistic pixel art, strict orthographic construction views; prioritize same-object geometric consistency and camera correctness.
project.gameplay_loop: Review consistent projections of scenery before 3D reconstruction.
project.session_goal: One valid three-view sheet with consistent length, height, depth and feature correspondence.
project.visual_reference_usage: North-star full-screen mock at project viewport resolution (3072x1024). Align palette, line weight, and mood with art_direction — not pixel-perfect. Do NOT use as img2img input for character/icon sprites; those use assets[].display_size on white studio.

asset.name: wood_three_views
asset.description: Create ONE TECHNICAL THREE-VIEW MODEL SHEET of the exact single knotted forked aquarium driftwood shown in the supplied artwork, using the supplied master image to identify the same object. This is a multi-view construction reference, not an attractive presentation illustration. Pure WHITE page, exactly THREE equal vertical panels in ONE HORIZONTAL ROW. Use small simple headers: FRONT above LEFT panel; RIGHT above MIDDLE panel; TOP above RIGHT panel. No extra views. Flat neutral diffuse light, no cast shadows, no horizon, no ground plane. Restrained source-matched painted pixel art, clearly readable contour and plane boundaries. Retain the thick knotted root crotch LEFT of center, the long shallow-S main limb rising to the RIGHT, one shorter UPWARD fork, the frayed left broken root, and the two downward stabilizing root branches. Every fork emerges from the same connected continuous wood body, same number and locations of branch junctions in all three projections. Approximate shared dimensions: LENGTH X = 55 cm, HEIGHT Y = 30 cm, front-back DEPTH Z about 22 cm. ALL THREE VIEWS are true ORTHOGRAPHIC parallel projections of ONE coherent physical object. FRONT: camera exactly level at object center looking along -Z, eye elevation ZERO; X horizontal and Y vertical. Show no top-facing area from camera tilt. RIGHT: Look exactly from the RIGHT END along negative X, so the long main limb points at the viewer and collapses into its broken irregular end cross-section. Horizontal size is DEPTH Z, about 40% of FRONT length; height is identical to FRONT. Root crotch sits behind the broken main-limb end, upward fork above it and stabilizing roots below, with some deliberate occlusion. Do not expose the full broadside trunk again. TOP: The root's FRONT-BACK spread must become visible. The long main branch extends left-to-right on the page. The UPWARD fork points toward the top camera and is therefore strongly FORESHORTENED to a short thick stub/root socket, not still shown as a towering vertical branch. The two stabilizing roots separate in DEPTH around the base. Paint upper wood surfaces only; this cannot be a copied broadside rotated within the page. Scale consistency: FRONT and TOP must have identical X LENGTH on the page; FRONT and RIGHT must have identical Y HEIGHT; RIGHT horizontal depth equals TOP vertical depth. Keep object centered in each panel; fit all silhouettes with white margin. The master reference is a three-quarter concept and MUST be rotated into these strict technical cameras. In TOP there must be NO long visible vertical facade. In RIGHT there must be NO long visible left-right facade. Do not copy the same silhouette three times. No isometric or three-quarter view in ANY panel. No redesign or extra branches. No perspective foreshortening except the disappearance of axes in the orthographic projection.

plan.prompt:
Create a BLACK PENCIL / GRAY CLAY ORTHOGRAPHIC ENGINEERING STUDY, NOT a colored illustration. Identify the exact connected object in the reference artwork and infer its physical 3D structure.
One connected forked root, about 55 cm long, 30 cm high and 22 cm deep: bulbous knotted crotch on left, long S-shaped horizontal trunk to the right, one short vertical upward fork, left broken root, and two downward roots whose feet spread in depth.
One white sheet, exactly 3 panels in a horizontal row: FRONT at left, RIGHT in middle, TOP at right. Use small plain labels above. Same world scale throughout. Simplified gray mass and thin black silhouette/structure lines ONLY, no wood grain, no mineral texture, no painted lighting, no isometric sketch.
FRONT: strict orthographic ELEVATION. Camera exactly horizontal at mid-height. X is horizontal and Y is vertical. Horizontal upper surfaces become edges with NO visible area from camera tilt. No perspective.
RIGHT is the actual narrow END PROFILE of the root. The 55 cm long trunk axis points STRAIGHT at the viewer so the long trunk is hidden behind its end face: an irregular broken OVAL cross-section is central, short vertical fork above it, crotch and root feet behind/below. Its width is about 22 cm, height 30 cm. There must not be a long horizontal stick in this panel.
TOP is an overhead MAP of the horizontal S-shaped trunk and root FOOTPRINT. The vertical upward fork is seen END-ON as an oval stub/socket, not as a branch sticking up the page. The two downward roots foreshorten and their separate footprints are visible. The vertical height must disappear in this top view.
The reference is an angled beauty illustration. Discard its camera completely. Output three actual CAD-style viewports of one coherent object. Align FRONT and TOP X extents; align FRONT and RIGHT height; RIGHT width equals TOP vertical depth. Show all silhouettes on white with margin. Spatial coherence is more important than rendering detail. No repeated broadside silhouettes. No scenery, no ground, no shadows, no colors, no extra views.
negative_hints: No isometric or three-quarter camera in any panel.
No colored texture, no scenery, no shadows.
Do not copy the source camera into TOP or RIGHT.
